mentions.description: This is a web-based accessible color palette editor that helps you create Tailwind-style palettes for web/UI design. Unlike tools that only take a single color and autogenerate or AI-generate the remaining tints and shades, it lets you tweak every tint and shade individually while keeping an eye on accessible contrast. A curve-based editor shows how the H/S/L values of your colors vary across a color scale, making editing quick and intuitive without giving up control to autogeneration.
mentions.problem: Most palette tools only let you enter a single color and then attempt to autogenerate or use AI to create the other tints/shades, which often don't do a great job and are really limiting when you're creating branded palettes.

mentions.problem: Hundreds of color palette generators exist, but most only let you customize a single color and autogenerate tints/shades without thought for accessibility or customization, and HSL-based pickers make accessibility tough because hue/saturation changes counterintuitively alter contrast checks.

mentions.description: This web tool creates custom Tailwind-style color palettes for web and UI design that pass WCAG contrast requirements. Its interface is optimized for exploring and tweaking multiple tints/shades at once, such as dragging vertically through the saturation curve or shifting whole curves horizontally. It uses the HSLuv color space so WCAG contrast stays constant when changing hue and saturation, and it can switch from the WCAG2 contrast checker to APCA, which corrects WCAG2 inaccuracies like being too forgiving for dark mode color combos. The desktop version has more features while the mobile version serves as a preview, and recent updates added more hints and tooltips.
mentions.problem: Creating accessible color palettes that pass WCAG contrast requirements is difficult, and the WCAG2 contrast checker is inaccurate in some cases, such as being too forgiving for dark mode color combinations.

mentions.name: Inclusive Colors
mentions.description: A web tool for creating custom color palettes for web designs that pass WCAG contrast requirements. Users can precisely tweak every shade and tint to incorporate their own brand colors (explicitly no AI or auto-generation) and build palettes with simple color contrast guarantees by design, such as all grade 600 colors having 4.5:1 WCAG contrast against grade 50 colors for body text. It exports to plain CSS, Tailwind, Figma, and Adobe, uses HSLuv for the color picker so only the lightness slider impacts WCAG contrast, and includes example open source palettes with hue, saturation, and lightness curves as design hints.
mentions.problem: Designers need color palettes for web designs that pass WCAG contrast requirements, and many design tools still use HSL, where WCAG contrast shifts unpredictably when any slider changes, making finding contrasting colors much harder.
mentions.audience: Advanced users creating color palettes for web designs; the author notes it is geared toward advanced users right now and hopes to simplify it with more handholding later.
